speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I see you have a chronic cough and a history of recurrent bronchitis. To understand the underlying cause, how many cigarettes or other tobacco products do you consume daily?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis. The patient's 11-year history of chronic cough with copious, thick, purulent sputum, morning exacerbations, and recurrent bronchitis despite being a non-smoker is highly characteristic of bronchiectasis. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CXR. REQUEST TEST: Sputum_Culture.
